title: The bread of life part 3
scripture_text: ‘’When they found him on the other side of the lake, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you get here?” Jesus answered, “Very truly I tell you, you are looking for me, not because you saw the signs I performed but because you ate the loaves and had your fill. Do not work for food that spoils, but for food that endures to eternal life. which the Son of Man will give you. For on him God the Father has placed his seal of approval.” Then they asked him, “What must we do to do the works God requires?”
devotional:
Jesus answered, “The work of God is this: to believe in the one he has sent. So they asked him, “What sign then will you give that we may see it and believe you?’ What will you do? Our ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness; as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from he haven to eat.’ Jesus said to them, “Very truly I tell you, it is not Moses who has given you the bread from heaven, but it is my Father who gives you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is the bread that comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” “Sir,” they said, “always give us this bread.” Then Jesus declared, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believe in me will never be thirsty. But as I told you, you have seen me and still you do not believe. All those the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never drive away. For I have come down from heaven not to do my will but to do the will of him who sent me. And this is the will of him who sent me, that I shall lose none of all those he has given me, but raise them up at the last day. For my Father’s will is that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in him shall have eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day.” John 6 v 25-40

‘’Jesus said to them, “Very truly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day. For my flesh is real food and my blood is real drink. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in them. Just as the living Father sent me and I live because of the Father, so the one who feeds on me will live because of me. This is the bread that came down from heaven. Your ancestors ate manna and died, but whoever feeds on this bread will live forever.” He said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum. it, many of his disciples said, “This is a hard teaching. Who can accept it?”

Aware that his disciples were grumbling about this, Jesus said to them, “Does this offend you? Then what if you see the Son of Man ascend to where he was before! The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing. The words I have spoken to you—they are full of the Spirit and life. Yet there are some of you who do not believe.” For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray him. He went on to say, “This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless the Father has enabled them.” From this time many of his disciples turned back and no longer followed him.’’ John 6 v 53-66

Jesus looks for their faith.

In verse 28-29 we read: -

“Then they asked him, “What must we do to do the works God requires?”

Jesus answered, “The work of God is this: to believe in the one he has sent.”

What is Jesus saying here?

Jesus is not saying that we are saved by doing work. But what he is saying is that these people must work at having faith.

When we think of believing we usually have a very narrow or precise understanding of what faith means. Let me explain, often we think as unbelief or doubt as the opposite of belief/faith. And they can be, especially when it comes to our understanding or reasoning. However, a better word to describe the opposite of the bible’s understanding belief/faith is independence. The Greek word John uses for belief pisteuō) means a lot more than mental assent. The word was used by the Greeks to mean “to believe in something” not just to believe facts about something. It meant to trust in; to have confidence in. It means to entrust oneself to an entity in complete confidence. To believe in with the implication of total commitment to the one who is trusted.

The interesting thing is this, Jesus describes the act or process of total dependence, i.e. believing as work. Why would he do that? I think most of us are uncomfortable with the thought of being dependent, we are happy with a ‘cerebral,’ faith, a faith that acknowledges, but we need a faith that depends.

To become people who are living dependent lives is never a default position, it is not something we would choose or want. We don’t like to look weak, or recognize that we are people in need. We need to cultivate an attitude of dependence. We need to work hard to become people who live as those who continually feel their need of God. Very early in Greek history, the word for work was associated with specific occupations like farming or being a soldier. It draws a picture of someone actively engaged in production or achievement. We need to become people who are actively engaged in becoming people who have an ever-increasing need of God. Cultivating dependence upon God at its essence is one of the ways we express our love for him.

The work of complete and total surrender of dependence is the best work any person can do, the word that describes this work is faith.

Let me just give one simple illustration of how we resist dependence and fight to hold onto our independence.

Do you ever find it difficult to ask for prayer? Sometimes it is the last thing we will do. We don’t want to become vulnerable, we want to protect our reputation of being able to cope. Prayer is a language of dependence.

The work of faith is not only developing dependence, but it is choosing to trust God irrespective of what circumstances we may be struggling with. It is trusting God in the face of uncertainty and confusion. Sometimes holding on to your faith can be very hard work.

There is a difference between depending on someone and using someone.

These people were looking for Jesus to use him to meet their need for bread. However, when it comes to dependence upon Jesus, it has more to do with love and devotion. Dependence upon Jesus is to acknowledge Jesus himself is our greatest need.
prayer: Father help me to cultivate real dependence on you.
